note: Per-country area and population, used only to normalise infrastructure length (km per 1,000 km², km per million people) so that countries of very different size stay comparable. Area comes from the CIA World Factbook and population from Eurostat for its reporting countries; the CIA World Factbook supplies population for countries outside Eurostat coverage. Serbia uses Factbook area and Eurostat population; Bosnia and Herzegovina and North Macedonia use Factbook area and population values. Both sources exclude Kosovo from Serbia, matching the Natural Earth outline in data/geo/countries/rs.geojson. The Factbook was retired in February 2026 and cia.gov no longer serves the country pages. Wayback snapshots of them do not help either: they captured only the page shell, because the figures were loaded client-side. The areas are therefore cited to factbook.json, the public-domain machine-readable conversion of the final (2025) edition, which is where these values were actually read and which still resolves. Cyprus uses the Factbook total less the 3,355 sq km it lists in north Cyprus, because Eurostat population and the Natural Earth outline in data/geo/countries/cy.geojson both cover the Republic of Cyprus only.
